findings.issue: Security's round-1 minor 1 is only partly closed. WithoutXff hides X-Forwarded-For, but Spring's ForwardedHeaderFilter (ForwardedHeaderUtils.parseForwardedFor) reads the RFC 7239 `Forwarded: for=` header first, and only then XFF. A request with `Forwarded: for=9.9.9.9` and no X-Internal-Client-Ip still sets getRemoteAddr() to 9.9.9.9, so ClientIp's socket-peer fallback can still be chosen by the caller. Nothing in the repo strips `Forwarded`. The reach is the same as in round 1 (direct in-cluster calls, or the gateway removing the header), and that caller can already set X-Internal-Client-Ip, so the impact stays low. Even so, the class javadoc ('stops ... turning a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For into getRemoteAddr()') and ADR 0002 line 49 ('X-Forwarded-For can never become that peer') overstate what the code guarantees.
findings.fix: In the wrapper, also drop the for= value of `Forwarded`, or keep the filter's host/proto and restore the original getRemoteAddr()/getRemoteHost()/getRemotePort() after super.doFilterInternal wraps the request. Restoring the peer is the more robust option because it covers both headers. Add a test case with `Forwarded: for=9.9.9.9` that asserts the socket peer is used.

findings.issue: The FilterRegistrationBean is registered whatever server.forward-headers-strategy is set to. Boot registers its own filter only under strategy=framework. Only Helm sets framework for auth (values.yaml:140), and auth's application.yml sets no strategy. So in compose/local, in tests, or if the Helm env is ever dropped, auth now honours client X-Forwarded-Host/-Proto/-Port/-Prefix and `Forwarded` when it did not before. Under NATIVE, Tomcat RemoteIpValve would also run alongside this filter. This is a silent behaviour change outside the documented deployment (it affects request URLs and {baseUrl} in the OIDC redirect template).
findings.fix: Annotate the bean or class with @ConditionalOnProperty(name = "server.forward-headers-strategy", havingValue = "framework"), matching Boot's own condition.

findings.issue: Replacing Boot's registration also skips Boot's ForwardedHeaderFilterCustomizer, which sets relativeRedirects from server.tomcat.use-relative-redirects. Auth does not set that property today, so nothing changes now, but the gap is not visible. Dispatcher types are fine: FilterRegistrationBean defaults a OncePerRequestFilter to all dispatcher types.
findings.fix: Accept an ObjectProvider<ForwardedHeaderFilterCustomizer> and apply it, or add a javadoc line saying customizers are not applied.

findings.issue: The test calls the filter directly. That Boot backs off rests on the CEO's reading of the Boot 4.0.7 source (evidence.md), not on a test, so a Boot upgrade that changed the condition would go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Optionally add a small context test with server.forward-headers-strategy=framework that asserts exactly one FilterRegistrationBean<ForwardedHeaderFilter> and that it wraps HostAndProtoOnlyForwardedHeaderFilter.

findings.issue: Leftover from round-1 nit 4. AuditInterceptor is auto-configured in every servlet service that has auditing enabled, but only the gateway, payment and user-service pin the strategy to none. On Kubernetes, the other servlet services keep Boot's NATIVE default, so their audit IP fallback (header absent) can still come from XFF through RemoteIpValve. This is inside the in-cluster trust boundary.
findings.fix: Pin SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none for every servlet service except auth in the Helm template (one default instead of per-service ifs), or narrow the ADR line 49 claim.

findings.issue: Round-1 nit 5 is still open: there is no pointer in the techdebt register to the Feign relay follow-up recorded in backlog.md and the ADR.
findings.fix: Optional one-line pointer, or say in the PR that backlog.md is the record.

summary: Delta b4abf171..690f934a. Status of the round-1 findings. Reviewer minor (env reference marking the referral salt and lookback as set by Helm): resolved. The values.yaml comment now uses property names and both rows show '-' again; the CEO-run env reference --check passes. Reviewer nit 2 (trailing-comma deviation): resolved at ADR line 43. Reviewer nit 3 (TD-SEC-15 wording): resolved. Reviewer nit 4 (NATIVE fallback): resolved for payment (Helm pins none) and for auth (new filter), but other servlet services that run AuditInterceptor still use NATIVE (nit). Reviewer nit 5 (techdebt pointer): still open, a nit. Security minor 2 (stale forward-headers docs): resolved in env-descriptions.json, environment-variables.md and the user-service application.yml comment. Security minor 3 (ADR gate scope): resolved; the B-4 release gate now names all four consumers. Security minor 1 (auth fallback under framework): mostly resolved. ForwardedHeaderConfig hides X-Forwarded-For from a ForwardedHeaderFilter subclass, so getRemoteAddr stays the socket peer for XFF, and host/proto still apply. The CEO's Boot 4.0.7 source check confirms that Boot's ConditionalOnMissingFilterBean(ForwardedHeaderFilter) backs off for a FilterRegistrationBean of the subclass, and the bean name does not clash because Boot's bean is never created. Two minor gaps remain. Spring's filter also takes the remote address from RFC 7239 `Forwarded: for=`, which is not hidden, and the filter is registered even when the strategy is not framework, which changes auth's forwarded handling in compose and tests. Neither is a new external bypass: both are reachable only when X-Internal-Client-Ip is absent, which is inside the documented in-cluster trust boundary. The two new tests prove the XFF case and that host/proto are kept. I found no regressions in the delta. Fix round 1 was verified by the CEO (forge-verify PASS, 293 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failures). No blocker or major findings, all ACs met: approve.
